body:
I think its might be the side effect of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104357, since the mrp works well after I revert the pr. (?

I thought roughly about how the problem happened. MRP calls menu_selector.set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(Control.PRESET_CENTER) and menu_selector.global_position.y = option.global_position.y - (menu_selector.size.y - option.size.y) * 0.5 + (4 if main_menu else 0) in turn.

When calling menu_selector.set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(PRESET_CENTER), the menu_selector is centered and minimized, with offsets set to 0 in all four directions. Subsequently, it was menu_selector stretched out due to the setting of the minimum size and growth direction, but this only changed its pos_cache and size_cache, and its offset in all four directions did not change (still 0). Since both growth directions are "both", the pos_cache is in the upper left of the center point.

The value of menu_selector.global_position.y was subsequently changed, which eventually recalculates the value of offset in the set_position. Prior to [this PR](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104357), the control used size_cache when recalculating the offset. After this PR, the size which is recalculated in real time via offsets is used instead. But the offset in all four directions is 0, and the calculated size is also (0,0), resulting in the final recalculated offsets will make the control being compressed to the size of (0,0) in the original pos_cache position. After that, again due to the setting of the minimum size and growth direction, the control expands around this position, and the pos_cache is changed again, its x and y values are both smaller than the expected.

The end result is that the position of the control is shifted to the top left of the expected position, and the value global_position set is not the same as the value when it was obtained
